narrative: The model estimated a 27% probability that you would be a bad credit risk—roughly one in four similar applicants would be expected to have repayment problems. Although that is not a majority, it was above the bank’s approval cutoff, so the application was denied. The three most influential factors in this decision were, in order: the amount requested, your employment duration, and your installment rate. Importantly, each of these worked in your favor by lowering the estimated risk. Your requested amount of 3,001 DM was very close to the approved applicants’ average of about 3,020 DM. Your employment history of four to seven years was also favorable and consistent with a stable income pattern. Your installment rate of 2.00 was below the approved average of 2.99, meaning the proposed repayment burden was relatively modest. The denial therefore reflects the overall combination of information, not these three factors alone: the favorable effects of the loan amount, job tenure, and installment rate were not enough to offset the rest of your profile. Next, ask the bank for the specific reasons and whether you can appeal or provide updated documentation. You could also discuss a smaller loan amount, adding a guarantor or co-applicant, strengthening savings, and avoiding new credit before reapplying.
